descriptive_title: Kindergarten Mathematics: Number Sense and Operations — Estimating to 20, Adding and Subtracting to 10, Equal Sharing, and Canadian Coins to 25¢ (A6.7–A6.13)
short_description: A 5-day Ontario Kindergarten unit on Number Sense and Operations (A6.7-A6.13), framed around Penny and Nick, two child-chef Coin Counters running a classroom snack shop, with Quincy the smiling piggy bank cheering them on.
long_description: Children spend a focused week becoming Junior Coin Counters — estimating, counting, adding, subtracting, sharing, and shopping. Day 1 'How Many in the Jar?' opens with Penny's estimation jar of pennies and a Coin Path floor mat for count-on practice (A6.7, A6.8). Day 2 'Plus and Minus to 5' uses snap-cube number bonds and a Partner Hunt game where one child hides cubes under their hand and the other names the missing partner — the K-appropriate route into A6.11 recall and the related subtraction. Day 3 'Snack Shop Story Problems' is the keystone: children listen to acted-out stories, decide whether to ADD or TAKE AWAY based on keyword cues, and model with cubes or coins, with a mid-unit Numerals 0-10 Check-In to flush out operation-choice errors before Day 4. Day 4 'Sharing Fairly' introduces equal-share through 'one for you, one for me' dealing onto paper plates, with a deliberate leftover round (7 grapes for 2 plates) that anchors the social-fairness conversation as much as the math. Day 5 'Penny, Nickel, Dime, Quarter' is the capstone: real Canadian coins, a Snack Shop with priced items (lollipop 5¢, popcorn 10¢, pizza 25¢), and the side-by-side dime-vs-nickel reveal that breaks the 'bigger means more' rule. Every lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough with three common K misconceptions paired with concrete recovery moves. Differentiation paths cover emerging, extending, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners. Mid-unit and end-of-unit formative + summative assessment artifacts included.
what_is_included: 5 fully-scripted lesson plans (40-50 minutes each, ~225 minutes of total teaching time)
5 student worksheets aligned to each lesson, with name/date fields and child-voice learning goals
1 mid-unit formative assessment (Numerals 0-10 Check-In) administered between Lessons 3 and 4

10 printable teacher manipulatives: Canadian coin set, estimation jar template, snap-cubes label, ten-frame mat, Snack Shop price cards, sharing paper plates, sharing objects kit, and three character puppets (Penny, Nick, Quincy)
1 end-of-unit reflection sheet with 5 self-assessment prompts
1 six-row summative rubric covering A6.7-A6.13 across 4 levels (Beginning, Developing, Achieving, Exceeding)
1 summative-administration guide tying the rubric to Lesson 5 worksheet, the lesson, and the rubric, together for the teacher
Junior Counting Crew certificate (one per child) for the closing ceremony, featuring Penny, Nick, and Quincy
Detailed expanded walkthrough for the keystone lesson (Lesson 3 — Snack Shop Story Problems), including the side-by-side dime-vs-nickel recovery move for the size-vs-value confusion
Differentiation tracks built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners
target_buyer: Ontario Kindergarten teachers (FDK or JK/SK split) covering the A6.7-A6.13 cluster of the 2026 K Math curriculum. Useful as a 5-day unit at the start of the calendar year (September-October) or as a money-and-operations review block before the Lunar New Year / Valentine's Day classroom-economy projects in mid-winter.
subject: Mathematics
strand: A. Foundations of Language and Mathematics — Number Sense and Operations
pedagogical_approach: Concrete-Representational-Abstract progression across the 5 days. Real coins and cubes anchor every concept before any worksheet abstraction. The keystone Lesson 3 uses the keyword chart as a meta-strategy that builds operation-choice fluency. Differentiation is proactive (built into every lesson) rather than remedial. Indigenous, Canadian, and FSL contexts noted in pedagogical_notes.
